ON 14MAY11, THE 74.8 FT. INSPECTED PASSENGER VESSEL LU-LU BELL IS HARD AGROUND IN PORT ETCHES NEAR ENGLISH BAY ON THE WESTERN SIDE OF HINCHINBROOK ISLAND. VESSEL GROUNDED WHEN THE VESSEL MASTER FELL ASLEEP AFTER GULF OF ALASKA TRANSIT FROM ELFIN COVE. VESSEL HAD ENTERED PORT ETCHES TO REST PRIOR TO CONTINUING TO VALDEZ FOR THE SUMMER PASSENGER VESSEL SEASON. THE TWO POB O/B AT TIME OF GROUNDING WERE REMOVED VIA CG-6014 WITH NO INJURIES. PROTECTIVE NOTICE ONLY AS REQUIRED BY USEPA. APPROXIMATELY 1300 GALLONS OF TRICHLOROETHYLENE WAS RELEASED BY AN UNATTENDED TRANSFER HOSE AFTER AN EMPLOYEE SUFFERED A SPLASH OF PRODUCT. THE MATERIAL WAS ALL RELEASED INTO A SPILL CONTAINMENT DIKE ON THE EMCO PROPERTY (OPEN TO AIR ONLY) AND WAS QUICKLY AND PROPERLY CLEANED UP. IT WAS ESTIMATED THAT APPROXIMATELY 600 POUNDS OF MATERIAL VOLATILIZED INTO THE AIR. EMCO DID NOT INITIALLY REPORT TO NRC BECAUSE IT BELIEVES THE RELEASE WAS NOT CHARACTERIZABLE AS BEING TO THE ENVIRONMENT BECAUSE THERE HAD BEEN NO RELEASE TO SOIL OR GROUND WATER AND THERE WAS NO EXCEEDANCE OF AIR QUALITY STANDARDS AT THE SITE BOUNDARIES. USEPA INSISTED THAT IT BE REPORTED TO THE NRC SO EMCO IS MAKING THIS PROTECTIVE NOTIFICATION. EMCO RESERVES ITS RIGHTS TO DEFEND AGAINST ANY ENFORCEMENT CLAIMS BY USEPA.

Medium Affected: WATER

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 32.556111, -85.532222 (Explicit)
Report Description
***THIS REPORT WAS RECEIVED VIA THE WEB REPORTING SYSTEM*** A FIRE WAS ACCIDENTALLY STARTED IN A MOBILE STORAGE CONTAINER (8X8X20 FT.). THE FIRE WAS INITIATED VIA THERMITE IGNITION. THE MOBILE FACILITY ALSO HAD SMALL QUANTITIES OF VARIOUS OXIDIZERS, METAL FUELS, AND METAL OXIDES USED AS ADDITIVES IN THE THERMITE MIXTURE. CURRENTLY, THE HIGH TEMPERATURES PREVENTED ACCESS TO THE CONTAINER TO ASCERTAIN THE COMPLETENESS OF THE INCINERATION. THUS, IT CANNOT BE DETERMINED IF THE QUANTITIES OF CHEMICALS WERE FULLY BURNED OR REMAIN ABLE TO BE RELEASED INTO THE ENVIRONMENT. THE CHEMICALS OF CONCERN AND QUANTITIES ARE: NICKEL POWDER (300 G), COPPER OXIDE (300G), LEAD OXIDE (50 G), VANADIUM PENTOXIDE (250G), BARIUM NITRATE (180G). IT IS BELIEVED THAT ALL QUANTITIES OF OXIDIZER WERE CONSUMED IN THE FIRE.
